newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's planning deep price cuts - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's planning deep price cuts - WSJ.

text.p: McDonald's Corp plans to begin its biggest discounting program to date by dropping the price of a Big Mac from $1.90 to $0.55 with the purchase of fries and a drink, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
Company Vice Chairman Jack Greenberg will pitch the move, which could set off a price war, to franchisees tomorrow via closed circuit videocast, the report said.
The report cited an internal document that said "McDonald's pricing isn't competitive" and that price cuts could turn around "the declining momentum of sales, transaction and cash flow."
A majority of franchisees in each market must support the plan for it to be approved, the paper said, adding that Greenberg has been lobbying franchisees for support in recent days.
The report said the 55-cent package will rotate from Big Macs to the company's other sandwiches and also promises to deliver sandwiches within 55 seconds of an order.
